analysis:
Examined docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 416-1210. The changed lines in these units are head 810-813 and 829. They document that GLM5Next video ingest now accepts variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks, read in presentation order. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate, matching the reference loader, where VFR video was previously refused with a 400. The text states that the existing bounds still apply: 2 FPS sampling, the 512 MiB maximumDecodedBytes decoded-frame cap, the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap, VisionMemoryGate reservation pricing and the video token ceiling. Media also remains excluded from prefix lookup and capture (permitsHybridCheckpoint), which keeps T-041 cache-sharing exposure unchanged. Processor refusals remain deterministic 400s.

The security-relevant question is availability (TB-007, ADV-002). Accepting VFR could change decode cost, for example a track with a skewed nominalFrameRate relative to its actual frame count. A frame-count/duration mismatch could then affect how many frames are decoded before sampling, even though only sampled frames are retained. The docs indicate the caps bound retained memory, but decode CPU time for non-sampled frames is not described. GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset source was not supplied. Integration should verify that the VFR path still enforces the frame-count, duration (maxVideoDurationSeconds 600) and decoded-byte caps. It should also verify that timestamp text derived from nominalFrameRate cannot produce an unbounded or zero/NaN rate (division by zero when nominalFrameRate is 0).

Head 1896-1899 (inline video labels in MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders) is in another batch. Its patch excerpt is truncated.

No concrete regression is evidenced by documentation alone, so no finding is raised. Deeper source review of the decode path is requested.
